 GUIDE: What to know before you vote in South Carolina 
 By WIS News 10 Staff Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 3:57 PM EDT | Updated : 11 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - Election Day is Nov. 3, as thousands will head to the polls across the country and in South Carolina.
 Here’s what to know before you vote.
 When do polls open?
 Polls open at 7 a.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 DECISION 2026
 Early Voting Data Interviews With Key S.C. Candidates When do polls close?
 Polls close at 7 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 3. If you are still in line by 7 p.m., you will be allowed to vote.
 Where do I vote?
 Click/tap here to check your voter registration and polling location. 
 Is there a sample ballot?
 Yes. Click/tap here to access your sample ballot.
 How do I vote absentee?
 Absentee ballots can be returned to your county voter registration office by mail or delivery by 7 p.m. on Election Day. 
 What do I need to bring?
 Per state law, voters are required to bring and present a valid photo ID before casting their ballot, which includes any of the following:
 South Carolina Driver’s License Includes standard license and REAL ID 
 South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles ID Card Includes standard ID card and REAL ID 
 Includes SC Concealed Weapons Permit 
 South Carolina Voter Registration Card with Photo 
 Federal Military ID Includes all Department of Defense Photo IDs and Veterans Affairs Benefits Card 
 US Passport Includes US Passport ID Card 
 What if I don’t have a valid photo ID?
 The South Carolina Election Commission says that if you don’t have a photo ID and are registered to vote, you can go to your county’s voter registration and elections office, provide information and have your photo taken. This can even be done on Election Day.
 Click/tap here for more information on photo ID policies in South Carolina. 
 Any other questions?
 Click/tap here for other frequently asked questions and answers provided by the South Carolina Election Commission.
